{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-wi-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"4356cda163244dfa54608ddf337495f3d4c66f15c219c15867c503b173676c03","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-wi-class-d:lineage:5","source_registry_sha256":"9dcfc0d0c3044debd01d4cb03103f48fb860797364a23b2cb56d36c868619a64","source_liveness_sha256":"4ca51030ff51b3372629ada1c05ad91f501dabccdcf7931dab678c717e7bb9b6"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Progression of licenses: documents, sponsorship, instruction permit, probationary license, regular license, transfers and REAL ID","heading":"C — Progression of licenses: application documents, adult sponsors, the instruction permit, the probationary (GDL) license, the regular license, out-of-state transfers and REAL ID","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Progression of licenses: application documents, adult sponsors, the instruction permit, the probationary (GDL) license, the regular license, out-of-state transfers and REAL ID
Knowledge domain: how a new Wisconsin driver moves from instruction permit to probationary license to regular Class D license — the documents to bring, who may sponsor a minor, who must ride along, how much supervised practice is required, the graduated license limits on hours and passengers, renewal timing, transfer deadlines and REAL ID.

FACT_ID: sec02-F01 | anchor: A01
The licenses described in this chapter are Class D, the non-commercial license for driving a car or light truck. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F02 | anchor: A01
You apply for a license in person at a DMV service center, bringing proof of your full name and date of birth, such as a U.S. birth certificate or passport. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F03 | anchor: A01
You also bring proof of U.S. citizenship or legal status, and a birth certificate or passport can serve for that as well. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F04 | anchor: A01
Proof of identity can be a signed Social Security card or a state-issued photo ID card, and showing the Social Security card also satisfies the identity requirement. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F05 | anchor: A01
Applicants must show two documents proving Wisconsin residence, such as a utility bill or a financial statement listing their name and Wisconsin address, and must provide a Social Security number. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F06 | anchor: A01
Every document must be valid, so photocopies and expired items are not accepted, and applicants must also meet physical and medical requirements. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F07 | anchor: A01
An applicant under 18 needs an adult sponsor to sign the Wisconsin Driver License Application, form MV3001. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F08 | anchor: A01
A sponsor accepts liability, which means being legally and financially responsible for incidents the minor causes while driving, and the sponsor can withdraw sponsorship at any time. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F09 | anchor: A01
The sponsor confirms that the applicant under 18 is enrolled in school and is not habitually truant, and later verifies the teen's practice driving hours. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F10 | anchor: A01
Sponsorship continues through the probationary phase until the driver turns 18. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F11 | anchor: A01
A parent, step-parent or legal guardian may sponsor a teen, and so may the sponsoring parent of a foreign exchange student. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0007]

FACT_ID: sec02-F12 | anchor: A02
When the teen does not live with a parent or legal guardian, a grandparent, aunt or uncle, foster parent, or a sibling or spouse who is 18 or older may sign as sponsor. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec02-F13 | anchor: A02
Some applicants under 18 file proof of insurance in place of a sponsor, including those with no living parent and those who live apart from their parents while studying full time or earning a living. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec02-F14 | anchor: A02
Proof of insurance also replaces a sponsor for a minor who is a ward of the state, county or court placed in foster or religious welfare care, or who is married to a spouse under 18. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0008]

FACT_ID: sec02-F15 | anchor: A03
You need an instruction permit to practice driving before the road test, and an applicant 18 or older qualifies by passing the knowledge test, the highway signs test and the vision screening. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F16 | anchor: A03
An applicant under 18 must also be at least 15 and enrolled in driver education, including its behind-the-wheel portion. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F17 | anchor: A03
The behind-the-wheel school gives the teen a signed MV3001 application, which must be completed before applying for the permit. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F18 | anchor: A03
A Class D permit holder may never drive alone; the companion must have at least two years of licensed driving experience and a valid regular license, not a probationary or occupational one. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F19 | anchor: A03
That companion sits in the front passenger seat and must be a qualified instructor aged 19 or older, a parent, guardian or spouse aged 19 or older, or any person aged 21 or older. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F20 | anchor: A03
When a parent, guardian or spouse is the companion, immediate family members of the permit holder may also ride in the back seat. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F21 | anchor: A03
If the permit holder is under 18, a companion aged 21 or older needs written permission from the minor's parent or guardian before the drive begins. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F22 | anchor: A03
A permit holder aged at least 16 may carry one more licensed person, aged 25 or older with at least 2 years of driving experience, in a seat other than the front seat. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F23 | anchor: A03
Driving in darkness on a permit requires either a qualified instructor or a licensed person aged 25 with at least two years of licensed experience in the seat beside you. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec02-F24 | anchor: A04
The probationary license is the first license issued after you pass the skills test, and you must be at least 16 to receive it. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F25 | anchor: A04
Phones may not be used while driving on a probationary license except to report an emergency. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F26 | anchor: A04
An applicant under 18 must hold the instruction permit for at least six months, be 16, and prove completion of driver education before getting the probationary license. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F27 | anchor: A04
Supervised practice on the permit must total at least 50 hours, made up of 40 daytime hours and 10 hours in darkness, with a qualified adult. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F28 | anchor: A04
Fifty hours is only the minimum, more may be needed to show safe driving, and the sponsor must verify the full 50 hours including the 10 after dark. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F29 | anchor: A04
Sponsors can print a driving log or use the RoadReady mobile app to track practice hours. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F30 | anchor: A04
The probationary license is also called a graduated driver license, or GDL, and its passenger and hour limits apply to drivers under 18 to cut distractions. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F31 | anchor: A04
The GDL limits last for the first nine months unless the driver turns 18 sooner, and no new license is needed when they end. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F32 | anchor: A04
Between 5 a.m. and 12 a.m., a GDL driver may drive alone anywhere and may carry any number of immediate family members. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F33 | anchor: A04
Between 5 a.m. and 12 a.m., a GDL driver may also carry one other passenger plus one licensed adult with at least two years of experience who is a qualified instructor or spouse aged 19 or older, or anyone aged 21 or older. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec02-F34 | anchor: A05
Between 12 a.m. and 5 a.m., a GDL driver may drive alone only when traveling between home, school and work. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F35 | anchor: A05
During those midnight-to-5 a.m. hours the same passenger limit applies: one qualifying licensed adult with at least two years of experience plus one other person. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F36 | anchor: A05
The GDL limits are extended by six months after a moving violation conviction, any breach of the limits, or a suspension or revocation for any reason. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F37 | anchor: A05
The handbook says points on second or later convictions double during this phase, as with the permit, and enough points on your record can cost you the license. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F38 | anchor: A05
The GDL hour and passenger limits stop applying once the driver turns 18. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F39 | anchor: A05
The regular driver license is the final step after the probationary license, and renewal can begin 90 days before the probationary license expires. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F40 | anchor: A05
A regular license must be renewed every eight years, renewal is allowed up to one year ahead of expiration, and it can be done online or at a service center. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F41 | anchor: A05
A renewal reminder arrives 45 to 60 days before your birthday in the year your license expires. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0011]

FACT_ID: sec02-F42 | anchor: A06
A new resident holding another state's regular license is an out-of-state transfer and should apply for a Wisconsin license within 60 days of moving. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F43 | anchor: A06
A commercial driver license holder from another state should apply for the Wisconsin CDL within 30 days of moving. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F44 | anchor: A06
A REAL ID from your previous state does not carry over, so you must present all acceptable documents again to get a Wisconsin REAL ID. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F45 | anchor: A06
A REAL ID meets U.S. Department of Homeland Security standards, and Wisconsin marks its REAL ID cards with a star. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec02-F46 | anchor: A06
Beginning May 7, 2025, flying within the U.S. or entering a military base or other federal building requires REAL ID-compliant identification or another accepted ID such as a passport. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0012]

Misconceptions: a sponsor is not just a signature, because the sponsor takes legal and financial responsibility and can withdraw at any time; the nighttime permit companion must be an instructor or an older licensed adult, not any adult; the GDL limits end at eighteen even if nine months have not passed, and they can be extended, not just completed; a REAL ID from another state does not transfer automatically.
Mnemonics: forty plus ten makes fifty supervised hours; the GDL night window runs from midnight to five in the morning; transfers are sixty days for a regular license and thirty for a CDL; renew every eight years.
Glossary: sponsor means the adult who signs a minor's application and accepts liability; habitually truant means repeatedly absent from school without excuse; instruction permit means the learner permit for supervised practice; probationary license means the first full license, carrying GDL limits for drivers under eighteen; GDL means graduated driver license; out-of-state transfer means a new resident licensed in another state; REAL ID means a federally compliant card marked with a star.
Dynamic facts: the document list, fees, the REAL ID enforcement date, renewal channels, the RoadReady app and the DMV web pages for sponsors and new residents can change; confirm them on the Wisconsin DMV website.
